title: Internal messaging runs on the native Rust fabric, never Pub/Sub or Kafka
statement: Internal publish/subscribe, durable event journals, control propagation and replay must use the Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric through its SDK and schema model. Google Pub/Sub and Kafka (including Managed Service for Apache Kafka) must not be internal runtime dependencies: neither may sit on the internal core path for service-to-service control, tick journaling, outcomes or replay.
rationale: The fabric exists so that control semantics, replay, partitioning, backpressure and regional independence are designed around the platform rather than around a generic broker's defaults. A managed broker on the internal path reintroduces semantics somebody else can change and a dependency the platform cannot fence per region.

title: Reflex Nodes publish through a non-blocking local ring/journal writer
statement: Each Reflex Node must embed a non-blocking fabric client: the decision thread writes durable outcomes, journals, telemetry and control acknowledgments into a preallocated, bounded local ring/append-only journal serviced on a separate core, and a separate drain forwards them asynchronously to the regional fabric. The fabric SDK must provide this local ring-buffer integration.
rationale: A publish call that can block moves the broker's latency and availability into the order path. Writing to a preallocated local structure and draining separately is what lets the fabric be durable without being on the hot path.

title: The fabric is never on the path from venue event to order
statement: No fabric acknowledgement, fetch or other synchronous call may sit between a venue market event and a local order decision or venue send: venue market data must reach the Reflex adapter directly and orders must go directly to the venue, never through a fabric topic. Control, outcomes, journals and telemetry are written after or beside the reflex decision, so a fabric outage, stall or failover cannot block, delay or retroactively stall market-event-to-order execution.
rationale: A fast broker in front of the hot path is still a dependency: its failover, a full quorum or a stalled segment becomes an order that went out late or not at all. Keeping the fabric beside the decision confines a fabric incident to journaling lag.

title: Reflex Nodes journal their decision history to regional fabric P1/P2 topics
statement: Each Reflex Node must asynchronously journal to its regional fabric every tick it acted on, feature snapshot, decision and decision trace, order, fill/cancel and outcome, and every control/policy/model acknowledgment: fills, cancels and outcomes to P1 Financial Outcomes topics; ticks, features and decision traces to P2 Market Journal topics; acknowledgments to the class their topic declares.
rationale: Replay and attribution can only reconstruct what was journaled. A cell whose fills reach the ledger but whose ticks and decision traces do not leaves every outcome unexplained.

title: Reflex Mesh coordination stays off the fabric
statement: Latency-sensitive peer coordination between Reflex Nodes (the Reflex Mesh) must travel directly peer-to-peer and must not be broker-mediated through the fabric, which carries only durable control, journal and outcome records; a fabric outage must not stop mesh coordination, and a mesh outage must not prevent durable journaling or control distribution.
rationale: Mesh messages are short-lived state whose value decays in milliseconds; fabric records are durable history. Carrying either on the other's path makes one pay for the other's guarantees and couples their failures.

title: Fabric records are durable and replayable
statement: Fabric messages must be durable, replayable records of control, journals and outcomes, under one native contract that also carries backpressure: every record accepted on a durable topic class must remain readable by partition and offset for that class's retention and be replayable to any authorised consumer, not delivered once and forgotten.
rationale: The platform's promise is that every decision is reproducible from the log. A bus that delivers and forgets can move control but cannot answer 'what did the cell know when it acted'.

title: The fabric distributes capital, risk and strategy control to Reflex Cells
statement: Capital grants, risk envelopes and strategy/model package activations decided centrally must reach each Regional Reflex Cell as P0 critical-control records delivered by its regional fabric — a centre-to-edge control path distinct from the cell's own asynchronous outcome reporting back to the fabric.
rationale: A cell can act only within an envelope it has actually received. Control that travels on an undeclared side channel has no offset, no replay and no record of what the cell was told and when.

title: Each region runs its fabric on dedicated broker VMs across three zones
statement: Each execution region must run its own fabric cluster — brokers and the metadata controller quorum — on dedicated regional Compute Engine VMs not shared with Reflex or warm-service workloads, spread across three zones so that the region has a three-zone quorum.
rationale: A broker sharing a host with trading compute or warm services shares their failures and noisy neighbours, and a quorum spread over fewer than three zones cannot survive a zone. A cluster per region is what makes one region's fabric independent of every other's.

title: Fabric sessions use QUIC with mutual TLS
statement: Every fabric session — producer and consumer (broker/client), inter-broker replication and cross-region mirror — must run over QUIC with TLS 1.3 mutual authentication by default, and a peer that cannot present a valid workload certificate must be refused.
rationale: The fabric carries risk envelopes, capital grants and fills. An unauthenticated session is a way to inject control or read financial outcomes; mutual TLS makes every session attributable to a workload identity.

statement: Every partition of a durable topic profile must be replicated with replication factor 3, the partition leader replicating to followers in the two other zones, so that each zone holds one replica.
rationale: Replicas that share a zone share its failure. RF3 across zones is what lets a whole zone go without taking a quorum-acknowledged record with it.

title: Only configured critical topics mirror across regions
statement: fabric-mirror must replicate across regions only the topics/partitions explicitly configured for mirroring — critical control and outcome streams — reading them from the local segment store; every other topic must stay in its region.
rationale: Mirroring everything turns each region's market journal into every other region's egress bill and backlog and makes a remote outage everyone's problem. Selective mirroring keeps what another region must know available there and nothing more.

title: Kafka and Pub/Sub compatibility exists only as a stateless edge bridge
statement: A Kafka, Pub/Sub or webhook compatibility adapter (fabric-bridge) may exist only where an external partner or client integration requires it, only at an external boundary and only as a stateless translator; internal services must use the native fabric protocol, and a bridge must not define or alter platform semantics (ordering, delivery, retention), which remain the fabric's.
rationale: A bridge that keeps state or that internal services can reach becomes the internal broker by the back door, and its semantics start to leak into contracts the fabric is supposed to own.

rationale: The append-only log is what every other guarantee (offsets, replay, archival, fencing) is defined against; a broker that rewrites or reorders its log breaks all of them at once.

title: Consumers checkpoint per-partition offsets and resume or replay from them
statement: Every consumer, including every fabric sink, must commit per-partition offsets (consumer checkpoints) to the fabric; after a restart or broker failover it must resume from its last committed offset, and any consumer must be able to replay a partition from any retained offset.
rationale: Offsets are what make at-least-once finite: without them a restart either loses records or replays the world. Replay by offset is how a sink recovers from a destination outage without a bespoke backfill.

The Raft-implementation choice is FABRIC-019, the no-cloud-database invariant FABRIC-020, separation from the data log FABRIC-065, ACL enforcement FABRIC-018, schema gating FABRIC-024 and producer fencing FABRIC-058. NEW_DEPENDENCY moves to FABRIC-019.

title: Every broker enforces topic ACLs from fabric metadata
statement: Every broker must authorise each produce, consume and admin request against the ACLs held in fabric metadata for the requesting workload identity and must refuse any request those ACLs do not grant.
rationale: An ACL recorded but enforced only at some brokers is enforced at none, because a client chooses its broker. Refusal by default is what stops an analytics workload writing to a P0 control topic.

title: The metadata quorum uses a mature Rust Raft implementation
statement: The fabric metadata quorum must use an existing, mature Rust Raft implementation for consensus rather than a hand-rolled one.
rationale: Consensus fails under partitions and timing that no fixture reproduces; a mature implementation has already met those failures in other people's clusters.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabric-controller row ('Metadata uses a Rust Raft implementation')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-meta ('mature Raft implementation')

notes: Merges three raw items (the controller row and the fabric-meta row, the latter stated twice). v2.1's 'mature' is the more specific wording and is kept; v11.6 says only 'a Rust Raft implementation'. This is the consensus class of ADR 0099 C2: until a record admits a Raft crate, ADR 0002 stands and this requirement is scored blocked on that record, not met by an in-tree implementation, because an in-tree Raft is what 'mature' excludes.

title: Regional fabric operation needs no cloud database
statement: A region's fabric (metadata quorum and brokers) must continue to operate with no cloud database reachable; fabric metadata must live only in its own quorum.
rationale: A fabric whose metadata sits in a managed database inherits that service's failure modes, and a database outage becomes a trading-region outage.

verification.check: With egress to every Google API denied on a regional test cluster, create a topic, move a leader, produce and consume, and assert all succeed.

notes: The raw extraction stated this twice from the same row. NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed: the requirement forbids a dependency rather than adding one. Archival to Cloud Storage is asynchronous (FABRIC-012) and so does not contradict this.

title: Each region stays independently writable; mirroring never blocks a local commit
statement: There must be no global or cross-region synchronous write quorum: each region's fabric must remain independently writable and operational, no local commit or acknowledgement may wait on a remote region's acknowledgement, and cross-region mirroring must be asynchronous, so that a remote-region or mirror-link outage cannot stop local execution, local journaling or control consumption.
rationale: A write that waits on another continent is only as available as the worst link in between. v11.6's stated reason: a remote outage must not stop local execution or control consumption.

title: Fabric contracts are versioned Protobuf schemas with immutable IDs
statement: Every fabric contract must be a versioned Protobuf descriptor held in the schema registry (fabric-schema) under an immutable schema ID and a schema hash, and every record on the wire must be encoded in the versioned Protobuf wire format (via prost) of the schema it names.
rationale: A record whose schema can be edited in place cannot be replayed faithfully. An immutable ID and hash are what let a replay decode last year's record with last year's contract.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabric-schema row ('Versioned Protobuf descriptors/contracts ... schema hashes')
§26.1 Protocol and semantics — Wire format ('versioned Protobuf via prost')

notes: Merges the fabric-schema rows (v11.6's stated twice) and the Phase 0 contracts clause with the wire-format clause. Compatibility gates are FABRIC-023 and FABRIC-024, code generation FABRIC-025. Protobuf via prost is the wire-schema class of ADR 0099 C2; ADR 0002 stands until its record exists, and the workspace's serde_json contracts are the permitted substitute to be scored against this.

title: CI rejects an incompatible schema change
statement: CI must check every fabric schema change against the backward/forward compatibility policy of the topic it serves and fail the build on an incompatible change.
rationale: Consumers of a topic are deployed independently of its producers; an incompatible change that merges breaks every consumer still on the old contract, and replay of old records with it.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabric-schema row ('compatibility checks')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-schema ('compatibility gates')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Schema evolution ('at CI and runtime registration')

verification.check: Submit fixture schema changes (remove a required field, renumber a field, change a field's type, add an optional field) and assert CI fails the first three and passes the fourth, proving the gate both refuses and admits.

notes: Split from v2.1 §7.1's 'at CI and runtime registration' because each gate is testable alone and each catches what the other misses: CI catches the reviewed change, runtime registration the one that never went through CI (FABRIC-024). v2.1 §25's 'Bad schema' game day (G p22) exercises both. NEW_DEPENDENCY (from the schema rows) is attributed to FABRIC-022 and removed here.

title: The runtime registry refuses an incompatible schema before any production topic sees it
statement: The schema registry must refuse, at runtime registration, any schema incompatible with the topic's compatibility policy, and every broker must refuse a record whose schema ID is not registered and compatible for that topic, so that no incompatible schema ever reaches a production topic.
rationale: CI is not the only way a schema reaches production. The runtime gate is what holds when a producer was built outside the pipeline or against a stale registry.

notes: The runtime half of the §7.1 schema-evolution clause, with the diagram's Meta/Schema authority over every broker as the enforcement point. See FABRIC-023 for the CI half.

title: Rust types are generated from the registered schemas
statement: fabric-schema must generate the Rust types producers and consumers use from the registered Protobuf descriptors, so the types in code and the descriptors in the registry cannot drift.
rationale: Hand-written types for a schema drift from it silently; generation makes the registry the one source of the contract.

notes: Stated in both blueprints' schema rows (three raw items). Code generation from Protobuf belongs to the wire-schema class of ADR 0099 C2.

title: Every archived segment carries a manifest, hashes, entitlements and a replay index
statement: Each segment fabric-archive exports must carry a manifest recording its topic, partition, offset range, content hash/checksum and entitlements, together with a replay index that locates records by offset without scanning the segment.
rationale: An archive that cannot prove its bytes are the ones the broker sealed, or say who may read them, is a pile of files; the index is what makes replaying one partition window cheap.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabric-archive row ('manifests, hashes, entitlements and replay indexes')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-archive ('Closed immutable segments + manifest/checksum')

verification.check: Archive a segment, then verify from its manifest alone that the stored object's hash matches, the offset range is complete and contiguous with its neighbours, entitlements are present, and the replay index resolves a sampled offset to the correct record; corrupt one byte and assert verification fails.

notes: Merges the fabric-archive rows (four raw items, two pairs of duplicates). Entitlements carry market-data licensing into the archive; licensing posture is evaluated before a source is used (data domain rule). MANAGED_SERVICE is removed: the manifest contract does not depend on where the object is stored.

title: Operators administer and inspect the fabric through a Rust CLI and admin API
statement: The fabric must provide a Rust operator CLI and internal admin API (fabricctl / fabric-inspect / fabric-admin) to create topics, set quotas and retention, and inspect stream and partition health, consumer lag, ACLs, mirroring state, replay progress and diagnostics.
rationale: A process nothing can see is a process nobody can operate. Operators need one tool that reads the same metadata the brokers act on, not a console view reconstructed from logs.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabricctl / fabric-inspect row
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-admin ('Create topics, quotas, retention ... diagnostics')

verification.check: Drive every CLI command against a test cluster and assert each read reports the partition health, lag and ACLs the metadata quorum holds, and each write (topic creation, quota and retention change) is reflected in metadata and enforced by the brokers.

notes: Merges the fabricctl row with the create/inspect half of v2.1's fabric-admin row. Partition moves, drain, repair and compaction are FABRIC-070, emergency isolation FABRIC-028, authenticated admin access FABRIC-071; NEW_DEPENDENCY and MANAGED_SERVICE move with the IAM clause to FABRIC-071. P1: operator tooling is not a named foundation exit, and the MVP can declare topics in configuration.

title: Operators can isolate a stream or partition in an emergency
statement: fabricctl must be able to isolate a stream or partition in an emergency — stopping further produce and/or consume on it without deleting it or its retained records — with the isolation recorded as an attributable operator action and reversible.
rationale: A poisoned producer or runaway consumer on one stream must be stoppable without stopping the cluster, and deleting the stream would destroy the evidence of what went wrong.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabricctl / fabric-inspect row ('emergency isolation')

verification.check: Isolate a partition while producers and consumers are active and assert produce is refused with an isolation error, other partitions are unaffected, retained records are intact, the action is recorded with the operator identity, and lifting isolation restores service.

notes: The raw extraction stated this twice from the same row. v11.6 names the capability without its semantics: 'without deleting retained records' follows from the hash-chained log rule (nothing may edit sealed history) and 'recorded as an attributable operator action' from the house auditability rule; both are readings, not blueprint text. P0 because it is a safety control.

title: A latency and throughput benchmark harness runs in CI
statement: fabric-bench must measure fabric latency (publish-to-quorum-acknowledgement and publish-to-consume) and throughput per topic class, and must run in CI and in game days so a regression is visible before merge.
rationale: The fabric exists partly for performance; without a measured baseline in CI, every design choice about it is an assertion.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabric-bench / fabric-chaos row
§30 Build Order — Phase 0 Foundations ('benchmark harness')

verification.check: The harness runs in CI against a three-broker test cluster, publishes p50/p99/p99.9 publish-to-ack and end-to-end latency and sustained throughput per class, and fails the job when a figure regresses beyond a committed threshold.

notes: Split from the fabric-bench / fabric-chaos row (the chaos half is FABRIC-030) and from the Phase 0 exit (M p41), which sets P0. v2.1's Fabric SLO row (G p15, 'publish quorum p99') names a figure the harness should publish. MULTI_REGION and NEW_DEPENDENCY, carried by the Phase 0 item, are removed.

title: Deterministic fault and partition testing gates fabric adoption
statement: fabric-chaos must inject broker, zone and network-partition faults deterministically (reproducible from a seed) in CI and in game days, and application services must not adopt the fabric until its chaos suite passes.
rationale: A fault test that cannot be reproduced cannot be debugged, and a fabric adopted before its failure behaviour is proven moves its unknowns into trading.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — fabric-bench / fabric-chaos row ('deterministic fault/partition testing used in CI and game days')
§26 Recommended Build Order — Phase 2 Rust Fabric MVP ('chaos tests before application adoption')

notes: Split from the fabric-bench / fabric-chaos row. G p22 is cited on verification for the MVP exit criterion that sets P0 and adds the adoption gate.

title: The SDK's producer and consumer APIs are zero-copy friendly
statement: fabric-client must offer zero-copy-friendly producer and consumer APIs over Rust-first buffers, so a record is not copied between the caller's buffer, the batch and the socket where the protocol allows.
rationale: Copies per record are the dominant cost at P2 market-journal rates; an API shape that forces them cannot be optimised later without breaking callers.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('Zero-copy-friendly producer/consumer APIs')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('Rust-first zero-copy buffers')

verification.check: Benchmark the publish and fetch paths with an allocation and copy counter and assert bytes copied per record stay within the committed budget.

notes: Split from the SDK rows of both blueprints. P3: a throughput optimisation with no correctness content; FABRIC-013 carries the typed API. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept because 'zero-copy buffers' usually means a buffer crate, which would need a record.

title: Idempotent producers: sequence numbers make retries duplicate-free
statement: Every producer must carry a producer ID and a per-partition sequence number on each record, and the broker must discard a retried record whose sequence it has already appended and refuse an out-of-sequence gap, so producer retries never create duplicates in the log.
rationale: Retries are how at-least-once survives a lost acknowledgement; without sequence numbers every retry is a potential duplicate fill in the log.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('idempotent producer sequencing')
§26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('idempotent producer IDs/sequence numbers')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('idempotent producer sequence')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('producer epoch/sequence prevents stale duplicate producers')

verification.check: Property test: for any interleaving of sends, lost acknowledgements and retries from one producer, the partition log contains each sequence number exactly once and in order.

notes: Merges the idempotent-producer clauses of both blueprints. Fencing of a stale producer epoch is FABRIC-058; consumer-side deduplication by event ID is FABRIC-042. NEW_DEPENDENCY (from the SDK rows) is removed: sequence numbers need no crate.

title: Consumer groups share partitions under metadata-held leases
statement: fabric-client must support consumer groups: a topic's partitions are divided among a group's members under consumer leases held by fabric metadata, each partition consumed by at most one member at a time and reassigned when its owner's lease lapses.
rationale: Two members consuming one partition apply its records twice and out of order; leases held by the quorum, not by the members, are what prevent it after a pause or partition.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('consumer groups')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-meta ('consumer leases')

verification.check: Property test over member joins, leaves and lease expiries: at every instant each partition has at most one owner, and every partition regains an owner within one lease period after its owner leaves.

notes: Merges the SDK's consumer groups (stated twice) with fabric-meta's consumer leases. P1: consumer scaling is GCP Phase 6. NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed as inapplicable.

title: Consumers subscribe without polling on the caller's thread
statement: fabric-client must offer asynchronous (push-style) subscriptions that deliver records to a consumer as they arrive, without the caller polling in a blocking loop.
rationale: A consumer that must poll trades latency against wasted fetches; a subscription lets delivery latency follow arrival.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('async subscriptions')

verification.check: A subscriber registered on a partition receives each newly appended record within the delivery budget without issuing fetches, and a slow subscriber is paced by flow control (FABRIC-080) rather than blocking the SDK's other subscriptions.

notes: Stated twice in the raw extraction. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept: 'async' implies an async runtime, which this repository has refused deliberately (blocking I/O with explicit timeouts; ADR 0099 C2 names the class). Until that record exists a blocking subscription on a dedicated thread is the permitted shape and the difference is scored.

title: The SDK emits OpenTelemetry signals for every produce and consume
statement: fabric-client must provide OpenTelemetry hooks so every produce and consume emits metrics and carries trace context, letting a trace cross a fabric hop.
rationale: A trace that stops at the fabric cannot explain a slow decision whose cause sat on the other side of it.

sources.section: §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('OpenTelemetry hooks')
§26 Recommended Build Order — Phase 2 Rust Fabric MVP ('OTel')

verification.check: Produce and consume through the SDK with an in-memory telemetry sink and assert the produce and consume counters and latency histograms moved and the consumer's span has the producer's span as parent.

notes: Stated twice in the raw extraction; G p22 is cited on verification for the MVP exit criterion. ADR 0026 rejected an OpenTelemetry crate; the hooks must be met through the export path ADR 0028 and ADR 0032 settled on, or through a new record. The flag marks that decision rather than presuming a crate.

title: Durable records use QUIC streams; datagrams only for lossy telemetry
statement: Durable records must travel on long-lived, reliable QUIC streams; unreliable QUIC datagrams may be used only for topic classes explicitly declared lossy telemetry.
rationale: A datagram can be lost without either side knowing; a control or outcome record sent that way has no durability guarantee whatever its topic says.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Transport ('long-lived streams for durable records and QUIC datagrams only for explicitly lossy telemetry classes')

verification.check: Assert the SDK refuses to open a datagram channel for any topic whose class is not declared lossy telemetry, and that P0 to P2 records are only ever written to streams.

notes: Stated twice in the raw extraction (the transport bullet and a split of it). NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept with FABRIC-009's transport class.

title: Records and segments carry CRC and content-hash integrity protection
statement: Records and segments must carry CRC protection and BLAKE3/content hashes, verified on append, replication, fetch and archival; a broker, replica, consumer or archiver that finds a mismatch must refuse the record or segment rather than pass it on or repair it silently.
rationale: A flipped bit in a fill record replays as a different fill forever. Integrity checked at every hop localises corruption to the hop that caused it.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Wire format ('BLAKE3/content hashes and CRC protection on records/segments')
§03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Segment Store node ('checksums')

verification.check: Property test: flipping any single bit of a record or segment, at rest or in flight, is detected at the next verification point and the corrupted unit is refused, while unmodified units always verify.

notes: Split from the wire-format bullet (whose Protobuf half is FABRIC-022 and whose memory-format half is FABRIC-038), merged with the diagram's segment checksums. v2.1 §7.1's frame header (G p8) names CRC32C; it is noted here rather than cited because the raw extraction left the frame header to the contract domain. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept for BLAKE3: ADR 0002 authorises in-tree SHA-256 and HMAC by name, not BLAKE3 (ADR 0099 C2), so a SHA-256 content hash would satisfy 'content hashes' without a record and BLAKE3 specifically would not.

title: Unversioned in-memory layouts never reach the network
statement: Hot in-process structures may use Rust-native zero-copy layouts, but only the versioned wire format may cross the network; no unversioned memory layout may be written to a socket.
rationale: A raw struct layout on the wire is a schema nobody registered; it changes with a compiler or field reorder and breaks every peer and every replay.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Wire format ('never leak unversioned memory formats onto the network')

verification.check: An architecture test asserts every type written by the SDK's send path and the brokers' replication and mirror paths is a generated schema type encoded by the wire codec, with no raw byte reinterpretation of in-memory structs on those paths.

notes: Stated twice in the raw extraction. NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed as inapplicable.

title: Order is strict within a partition and never promised globally
statement: The fabric must deliver records in strict append order within each partition and must not promise, expose or imply a total order across partitions or regions; a consumer needing cross-partition order must derive it from record metadata (FABRIC-040).
rationale: A total global order is either false or a global quorum. Promising it invites consumers to depend on an ordering the system cannot keep.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Ordering ('strict per-partition order. No false promise of a total global order')

verification.check: Property test over concurrent producers and consumer restarts: each consumer observes each partition's records in exactly offset order; inspection of the SDK API finds no call that claims a cross-partition order.

notes: Split from the ordering bullet, whose metadata half is FABRIC-040. MULTI_REGION is removed: the property holds within one region.

title: Every record carries time, placement, epoch and hybrid-logical-clock metadata
statement: Every fabric record must carry its source event time, receive time, region, partition, leader epoch, offset and hybrid logical clock (HLC) timestamp.
rationale: Without the source/receive pair a replay cannot say what was knowable when; without leader epoch and offset it cannot say which leader wrote a record; without an HLC it cannot order records across partitions honestly.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Ordering ('Every record carries source event time, receive time, region, partition, leader epoch, offset and hybrid logical clock metadata')
§27 Core Contracts Between Brains — FabricEnvelope

verification.check: Property test: every record read back from any partition has all seven fields populated, offsets are dense per partition, leader epoch never decreases along a partition, and HLC timestamps never decrease along a partition across leader changes.

notes: Stated twice in the raw extraction. M p38's FabricEnvelope restates these fields among others (producer ID/sequence, priority/QoS, trace ID, idempotency key, payload hash, auth context) and is cited on verification; the envelope as a whole is left to the contract domain. v2.1's Rule 3 (G p3) and frame header (G p8) give overlapping field lists. The source/receive pair is what the data domain's bitemporal rule needs. MULTI_REGION is removed.

title: Durable streams deliver at least once; at-most-once is for telemetry only
statement: Delivery on every durable stream must be at-least-once to consumers by default, and at-most-once delivery may be configured only for telemetry classes.
rationale: At-most-once loses records by design. That is acceptable for a debug trace and never for a fill or a risk envelope.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('at-most-once allowed only for telemetry; at-least-once is default for durable streams')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('at-least-once to consumers')

verification.check: Property test over crashes of producer, leader and consumer at arbitrary points: every quorum-acknowledged record on a durable topic is delivered to each consumer group at least once; and topic creation refuses an at-most-once profile on any non-telemetry class.

notes: Merges v11.6's delivery bullet (stated twice in the raw extraction) with v2.1 §7.1's at-least-once clause.

title: Records carry deterministic event IDs and consumers deduplicate on them
statement: Every record must carry a deterministic event ID, stable across retries of the same source event, and consumers must deduplicate redelivered records by event ID together with partition sequence and fencing epoch.
rationale: At-least-once delivery means duplicates are normal; a deterministic ID is what lets every consumer recognise one without shared state.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('deterministic event IDs')
§2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('Consumers use event IDs, partition sequence and fencing epochs')

verification.check: Property test: re-producing the same source event yields the same event ID, and a consumer fed any sequence with duplicates and replays applies each event ID's effect exactly once.

notes: Merges v11.6's deterministic event IDs with v2.1 Rule 4's consumer mechanism (two raw items). Financial writers' transactional uniqueness is FABRIC-044.

title: No global exactly-once claim: effectively-once comes from idempotency and fencing
statement: Neither the fabric nor any documentation or API built on it may claim global exactly-once delivery; effectively-once processing must be achieved only as at-least-once transport plus idempotent producers, deterministic event IDs, idempotent state transitions and sinks, and fencing.
rationale: A claimed exactly-once guarantee makes consumers skip deduplication, and the first lost acknowledgement then books a fill twice.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('provide effectively-once processing with idempotent sinks')
§2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('Do not claim magical global exactly-once')
§28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — 'Claiming global exactly-once delivery'

verification.check: Inspection of the SDK, broker and sink documentation and API names finds no exactly-once delivery claim, and the effectively-once property is instead proven by the tests of FABRIC-042 and FABRIC-044.

notes: Merges v2.1 Rule 4 (stated twice in the raw extraction), the §28 anti-pattern and v11.6's 'effectively-once'. NEW_DEPENDENCY (from the anti-pattern) is removed as inapplicable. A mechanical documentation check would need to match the delimited claim, not the substring (house testing rule), which is why the method is inspection.

title: Financial outcome consumers commit each event once in effect, transactionally
statement: Every consumer that writes financial state — the ledger writer/sink above all — must be idempotent, enforcing uniqueness of the event ID transactionally in the same commit as the state change, so a financial outcome delivered any number of times is committed exactly once in effect.
rationale: The ledger is where a duplicate becomes money. Uniqueness enforced outside the transaction leaves a window in which a crash commits the change without the guard.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('idempotent sinks')
§2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('financial writers enforce uniqueness transactionally')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('Financial consumers are idempotent')
§21.1 Tick to order and learning — step 4 ('commit financial outcomes idempotently to Spanner')

verification.check: Property test: feed the ledger sink every P1 record of a session with arbitrary duplication, partition replays and crashes between the state write and the offset commit, and assert the resulting positions and cash equal those from a single clean delivery.

notes: Merges the financial-writer clauses of Rule 4, §7.1 Delivery, v11.6's idempotent sinks and §21.1 step 4. G p23 §27's 'committed exactly once in effect to Spanner' is the ledger domain's acceptance criterion and is not cited here. MANAGED_SERVICE and NEW_DEPENDENCY come from the Spanner step and are kept for that target; ADR 0099 C4 leaves the ledger store to its own record, and this invariant holds for whatever store that record picks.

title: P0 Critical Control topics: RF3 quorum, persistent WAL, long retention and archive
statement: Topics of class P0 Critical Control — risk envelopes, model activation, kill/fence commands and capital grants — must acknowledge a write only after an RF3 three-zone quorum has persisted it, with control metadata and the log held in a persistent write-ahead log, and must be retained long-term with every sealed segment archived to Cloud Storage.
rationale: These records decide what a cell may do. Losing one leaves a cell trading on an envelope that was withdrawn, and not keeping them makes 'what was the cell allowed to do' unanswerable afterwards.

§2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('Control and outcomes get quorum durability')

ADR 0089 already makes every event-log topic declare a retention class; the kill-switch engagement/release pair it fixed are P0 records in this taxonomy.

title: P1 Financial Outcomes topics: RF3 quorum, idempotent IDs, long hot retention and immutable archive
statement: Topics of class P1 Financial Outcomes — fills, cancels, position deltas and settlement events — must acknowledge only on an RF3 quorum, carry idempotent (deterministic) event IDs, keep long hot retention and archive every sealed segment immutably.
rationale: Outcomes must outlive a ledger outage in the fabric (v2.1 §22: outcome partitions accumulate durably while Spanner is down) and must remain provable afterwards from an archive nobody can edit.

§2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6
§7.2 Fabric topic classes — P1 Financial Outcomes row

notes: Merges v11.6's financial-outcome durability class and Rule 6 (each stated twice in the raw extraction) with the §7.2 P1 row. The row's 'ledger sink retries indefinitely' is FABRIC-082. MANAGED_SERVICE is kept for the archive's Cloud Storage target.

title: P2 Market Journal topics: RF3 regional quorum, batch producers, tiered hot retention, GCS archive
statement: Topics of class P2 Market Journal — ticks, books, features and decision traces — must replicate on an RF3 regional quorum with batching producers as high-throughput replicated segments, keep hours to days of hot retention set by instrument tier, and archive sealed segments to Cloud Storage.
rationale: The market journal is the platform's largest stream and the input to every replay; it needs throughput-shaped replication and a tiered hot window rather than control-grade retention on every tick.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Durability classes ('market journals use high-throughput replicated segments')
§7.2 Fabric topic classes — P2 Market Journal row

notes: Merges v11.6's market-journal durability class (stated twice in the raw extraction) with the §7.2 P2 row. The row's 'throttles mirror before local ingest' is FABRIC-083. P0 because canonical tick capture and deterministic replay are mandatory in master Phase 1.

title: P4 Telemetry topics: best effort or RF2, sampled or dropped oldest-first under pressure
statement: Topics of class P4 Telemetry — metrics-derived events and debug traces — may be acknowledged best-effort or on RF2, and under pressure must be sampled or drop their oldest records first, with every drop counted.
rationale: Telemetry is the pressure valve: it is the class that gives way so control and outcomes do not. Dropping oldest-first keeps the most current picture, and counting drops keeps the loss visible.

notes: Merges v11.6's telemetry durability class and Rule 6's telemetry clause (each stated twice in the raw extraction) with the §7.2 P4 row. The row's 'direct OTel remains primary health path' is FABRIC-073, which carries its NEW_DEPENDENCY. 'Every drop counted' is the house observability rule, not blueprint text. title: Every stream has explicit byte and message quotas, lag limits and an overload policy
statement: Every stream must be configured with explicit byte and message quotas (including per-producer quotas), consumer lag limits and a declared overload policy, and the brokers must enforce them.
rationale: A stream with no quota lets one runaway producer consume the broker every other stream depends on; an undeclared overload policy means the broker decides what to lose.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Backpressure ('every stream has explicit byte/message quotas, lag limits and overload policy')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('per-producer quotas')

verification.check: Exceed a producer's byte quota, then its message quota, and let a consumer fall past its lag limit, and assert each triggers the stream's declared overload action, is counted, and leaves other streams unaffected.

notes: Split from v11.6's backpressure bullet, merged with v2.1's per-producer quotas. v2.1's bounded queues are FABRIC-063, its credit/window flow control FABRIC-080 and its topic priority FABRIC-051.

title: Critical control and outcome records are never silently dropped
statement: Under backpressure or overload, P0 control and P1 outcome records must never be silently dropped: when the fabric cannot accept one, the producer must receive an explicit refusal it can act on, and nothing already acknowledged may be discarded.
rationale: A silently dropped kill command or fill is worse than a refused one, because the producer believes it was delivered and nothing downstream knows to look for it.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Backpressure ('Critical control/outcomes cannot be silently dropped')
§7.2 Fabric topic classes — P0 Critical Control row ('never intentionally dropped')

verification.check: Drive a broker into overload with mixed traffic and, by reconciling producer-side send logs against the partitions, assert every P0 and P1 send either appears in the log or received an explicit refusal — none vanished.

notes: Merges v11.6's backpressure clause (stated twice in the raw extraction) with the P0 row's 'never intentionally dropped'. MANAGED_SERVICE and NEW_DEPENDENCY, carried by the P0 row, are removed as inapplicable to this clause.

title: Telemetry and ambient signals are shed before control or outcomes are starved
statement: Topic priority must order shedding: under pressure, P4 telemetry and low-value ambient signals must be sampled or shed before any P0 control or P1 outcome traffic is delayed or starved.
rationale: Starvation is loss by another name: a risk envelope that arrives after the move it was meant to constrain did not arrive.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Backpressure ('telemetry and low-value ambient signals can be sampled or shed')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('Low-priority telemetry is sampled/dropped before control/outcome traffic is starved')

notes: Merges v11.6's shedding clause with v2.1 §7.1's topic-priority clause (stated twice in the raw extraction). FABRIC-050 is the no-silent-loss half; this is the no-starvation half, and each is testable alone.

title: Cross-region mirror traffic stays on private networking
statement: Cross-region mirror traffic must travel only over Google private networking, with the mirror prefixes explicitly exported through the latency NCC hub and no other cross-region route.
rationale: Control and outcomes crossing the public internet are exposed and their latency unbounded; exporting only the mirror prefixes keeps the rest of each fabric network unreachable from other regions.

sources.section: §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Cross-region behavior ('over Google private networking')
§7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — IP identity ('Cross-region mirror prefixes are explicitly exported through the latency NCC hub')

verification.check: terraform plan shows the mirror prefixes as the only fabric prefixes exported to the latency NCC hub, and no public route or external IP on any mirror endpoint.

notes: Split from v11.6's cross-region bullet (whose non-blocking half is FABRIC-021) and v2.1's IP-identity bullet (whose internal-address half is FABRIC-089). P1 with multi-region (master Phase 4, GCP Phase 7).

title: The fabric carries package announcements, never the packages
statement: For model and policy packages the fabric must carry only version, digest, availability and activation messages; the packages themselves must be stored as immutable signed artifacts in object/artifact storage and never carried on the fabric.
rationale: Large artifacts on the fabric would compete with control traffic for quota and replication, and would make the log, rather than signed storage, the place a package's integrity is established.

sources.section: §26.1 Hot-path contract — 'the fabric carries only version/digest/availability/activation messages'

verification.check: An acceptance test asserts every schema registered for a package topic holds only version, digest, availability and activation fields within a bounded record size, and a node activates a package only after fetching the artifact from storage and verifying its digest and signature.

notes: From v11.6's hot-path contract. Who may publish activations is FABRIC-111. P0 because Reflex runs signed packages from master Phase 1.

title: When the fabric is unavailable a node runs on its last valid package within a bounded local journal
statement: If its regional fabric is unavailable (including loss of quorum or of the whole regional fabric), a Reflex Node must continue under its last valid cached signed control package and its local journal, stop accepting new control changes, queue durable publications locally within a bounded disk budget, and degrade as policy defines before the journal is exhausted and no later than the package's TTL or the point its risk policy requires.
rationale: Stopping on a fabric outage would put the fabric back on the hot path by another route; carrying on forever would trade on a stale envelope and fill the disk. A bounded, policy-driven degradation is the middle the blueprint asks for.

sources.section: §26.1 Hot-path contract — 'a node continues under its last valid package and local journal until the package TTL or risk policy requires degradation'
§28 Failure and Degradation Model — Regional Event Fabric quorum lost row

notes: Merges the hot-path contract's fallback, the §31 cached-package clause (split from the item whose other halves are FABRIC-002 and FABRIC-003) and the region-loss row's Reflex clause. Fail-closed reading: an expired package narrows or halts; it is never extended. MULTI_REGION and NEW_DEPENDENCY, carried by the region-loss item, are removed.

title: Broker loss moves leadership to an in-sync follower; producers and consumers carry on
statement: On the loss of a broker, leadership of each partition it led must move to an in-sync follower in another zone; producers must refresh the partition map from metadata and retry by producer epoch, consumers must resume from their committed offsets, and Reflex execution must not wait for the failover.
rationale: A broker will be lost; what matters is that leadership moves to a replica that has every acknowledged record, and that clients follow it without duplicates or gaps.

sources.section: §28 Failure and Degradation Model — Regional Event Fabric broker loss row
§17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Fabric broker row

notes: M p40 is cited on verification and is the more specific wording ('in-sync replica in another zone', 'retry by epoch', 'resume from committed offsets'). v2.1's recovery half ('replace broker and rebalance') is FABRIC-098 and its 'quorum-acked records preserved' FABRIC-077. NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed as inapplicable.

title: Mirror lag has an independent, visible, bounded budget
statement: Each cross-region mirror must run to its own lag budget — its lag never back-pressures local commit or other mirrors — and its lag must be measured, visible and bounded, with a breach of the budget raised rather than absorbed.
rationale: A mirror that lags silently makes other regions act on stale control while believing it current; a budget turns lag into an alarm.

sources.section: §28 Failure and Degradation Model — Cross-region fabric mirror down row ('Mirror lag is visible and bounded')
§7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-mirror ('independent lag budget')

notes: Split from the fabric-mirror row (stated twice in the raw extraction); M p40 is cited on verification. Its consumer half ('Global consumers mark remote knowledge stale and replay ... when connectivity returns') is left to the resilience domain. NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed as inapplicable.

title: Every stream declares its class and semantics; nothing rests on broker defaults
statement: Every durable stream must be created with an explicit QoS class (P0 to P4) and declared partitioning key, ordering, retention, replication, overload and mirroring semantics, and the fabric must refuse to create a stream that leaves any of them to an unspecified broker default; durability is set per topic by its class, never globally.
rationale: A default is a decision nobody made. A stream whose retention or overload behaviour is whatever the broker ships with will lose the wrong records on the worst day.

sources.section: §31 Capability Completeness Checklist — 'Every durable event stream declares partitioning, ordering, retention, replication, overload and mirroring semantics'
§2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('Durability is per topic')
§7.2 Fabric topic classes

notes: Merges the §31 checklist item with Rule 6's 'durability is per topic' (the rule's per-class consequences are split into FABRIC-045 to FABRIC-048 and FABRIC-059). ADR 0089 already makes every event-log topic declare a retention class, which is one of the declarations required here, on the log the repository has.

title: Producer fencing: a stale producer epoch is refused
statement: Fabric metadata must assign each producer an epoch, and every broker must refuse writes from a producer whose epoch is older than the current one for its producer ID, so a zombie or superseded producer cannot append after its successor has started; P0 control topics must require producer fencing.
rationale: A paused process that wakes and resumes writing is how a superseded risk envelope or a withdrawn capital grant comes back. Fencing makes the successor's first write the predecessor's last.

§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('producer epoch/sequence prevents stale duplicate producers')

MANAGED_SERVICE and NEW_DEPENDENCY, carried by the P0 row and the anti-pattern, are removed as inapplicable.

title: P3 Intelligence/Research topics: configurable RF2/3, throughput batching, replayable backlog
statement: Topics of class P3 Intelligence/Research — evidence deltas, episodes and training candidates — must be replicated RF2 or RF3 by configuration, batched for throughput, replayable, allowed to accumulate backlog within their declared retention rather than shed, and served by consumers that scale out.
rationale: Research streams are large and tolerant of delay but not of loss: an episode dropped under pressure is a lesson the platform never learns.

sources.section: §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('research streams optimize throughput')
§7.2 Fabric topic classes — P3 Intelligence/Research row

verification.check: Stall P3 consumers for a sustained interval and assert no P3 record is shed, the backlog stays within the topic's retention, and adding consumers drains it.

notes: Merges Rule 6's research clause (stated twice in the raw extraction) with the §7.2 P3 row. 'Backlog allowed' is read within the house bounded-retention rule: consumers may lag within the declared retention, not without limit. P1 because the cognitive data loop is master Phase 2.

title: Each region's fabric lives in its own project: VPC, broker VMs, journal disks, archiver identities
statement: Each region's fabric must be provisioned in a dedicated prod/fabric-<region> project holding the fabric VPC, broker VMs, journal disks and archiver service identities, separate from the execution (Reflex) and services projects, so that a messaging failure or misconfiguration cannot directly reconfigure trading compute.
rationale: v2.1's stated reason: messaging failure cannot directly reconfigure trading compute. A project boundary is an IAM boundary, which a shared project is not.

sources.section: §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model — prod/fabric-<region> row

verification.check: terraform plan shows one fabric project per region containing the fabric VPC, broker VMs, journal disks and archiver identities, and no IAM grant giving a fabric identity any role on that region's execution project.

notes: P0 because the project model is GCP Phase 0 (org/folders/projects). ADR 0099 C8 governs when any fabric VM exists. The per-region Fabric VPC is also named in §3 (G p3).

title: The fabric implements only the semantics the platform needs, each proven by fault or property tests
statement: The fabric must implement only the semantics the platform requires — it is not a feature-for-feature Kafka clone — and each semantic guarantee it offers must be proven by a fault-injection or property test before anything relies on it.
rationale: Every guarantee copied without need is surface to maintain and a guarantee someone will eventually depend on without its having been proven.

sources.section: §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — introduction ('not a clone of Kafka feature-for-feature. It implements only the semantics the platform needs')
§28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — 'Rebuilding Kafka semantics blindly'

verification.check: Inspection maps every guarantee in the fabric's specification (ordering, delivery, durability per class, fencing, backpressure, mirroring) to at least one named property or chaos test that has been mutation-verified; a guarantee without one fails review.

notes: G p7's introduction is cited on verification; it states the same rule as the §28 anti-pattern. The mutation clause is the house testing rule. NEW_DEPENDENCY (from the anti-pattern) is removed as inapplicable.

title: fabricd is directed onto the Tokio async runtime
statement: fabricd must be built on an async runtime, which v2.1's implementation direction names as Tokio.
rationale: v2.1 chooses an async runtime for a broker holding many concurrent sessions; the choice decides the shape of every broker and SDK API, so it has to be settled before either is written.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabricd ('Tokio async runtime')

verification.check: Inspection of the dependency record admitting an async runtime and of fabricd's crate: the runtime is the recorded one and no other executor is present.

notes: Stated twice in the raw extraction. Conflicts with standing decisions: the workspace has no async runtime by choice (blocking I/O with explicit timeouts) and permits serde and serde_json only (ADR 0002, ADR 0009). ADR 0099 C2 names this class; until its record exists the broker is built on blocking I/O with timeouts and this requirement is scored blocked rather than quietly substituted. It is an implementation direction, not a correctness property, and is P0 only because the broker is a GCP Phase 2 deliverable and the choice must be settled first.

title: Broker memory is bounded: pooled buffers and bounded queues
statement: fabricd must allocate from bounded memory pools and hold every in-flight queue to a fixed bound, so overload produces backpressure or refusal rather than unbounded memory growth.
rationale: A broker that absorbs overload in memory fails all at once, taking every stream on it down together, which is the failure backpressure exists to prevent.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabricd ('bounded memory pools')
§7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('bounded queues')

verification.check: Freeze a sink and fill consumer lag (v2.1 §25's broker-backpressure game day, G p22) and assert broker resident memory stays under its configured ceiling throughout.

notes: Split from the fabricd row and the §7.1 backpressure bullet. Bounded working sets are a standing house rule; this is that rule for the broker. NEW_DEPENDENCY (from the fabricd row) is removed as inapplicable.

title: Journal I/O mode is chosen by benchmark
statement: Whether fabricd uses direct or buffered I/O for its journal must be decided by benchmark on the target disks, with the choice and its measurement recorded.
rationale: The right I/O mode depends on the disk and the workload; choosing it by assumption leaves throughput or tail latency on the table in a way nobody can see.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabricd ('direct/buffered I/O chosen by benchmark')

verification.check: fabric-bench runs append and fetch workloads under both I/O modes on the target disk type, and the recorded choice matches the better measured p99 at the required throughput.

notes: Split from the fabricd row. P3: an optimisation.

title: Metadata is kept separate from the data log
statement: Fabric metadata (membership, partition maps, epochs, leases, quotas, ACLs) must live in the metadata quorum's own replicated log, separate from partition data logs.
rationale: Metadata sharing a log with data would queue a leader election behind a burst of ticks and lose control of the cluster exactly when data pressure is highest.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-meta ('metadata separated from data log')

verification.check: With a data partition's disk full, assert metadata operations (leader election, ACL change) still commit; and inspection shows no metadata record type in any partition log.

notes: Split from the fabric-meta row (stated twice in the raw extraction). NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed as inapplicable.

title: Producers batch records for throughput
statement: fabric-client must batch records per partition in the background of the caller, within a bounded batch size and a bounded linger time.
rationale: Per-record round trips cannot carry P2 market-journal rates; unbounded batching would turn throughput into latency without limit.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('async batching')

verification.check: A throughput benchmark shows batched produce reaching the P2 class's target rate, and a test asserts no batch exceeds its size bound or lingers past its time bound.

notes: 'Async' is read as asynchronous to the caller (a bounded background flush), which a blocking-I/O thread can provide without an async runtime; the runtime question is FABRIC-062's, so NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed. P2 Market Journal's batch producers (FABRIC-047) depend on this.

title: Producers choose an explicit acknowledgement profile no weaker than their topic's class
statement: Every produce must use an explicit acknowledgement profile (for example quorum, leader-only or none), and the SDK must refuse a profile weaker than the topic class's declared durability requires.
rationale: Without the refusal a producer could publish P0 control at leader-only acknowledgement and the class's RF3 quorum would be a label.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('explicit ack profile')

verification.check: For each class, the SDK accepts the profile the class requires and refuses every weaker one (for example leader-only on P0) with an error naming the class.

notes: Split from the fabric-client row. The refusal of a weaker profile is the house fail-closed reading of 'explicit'. NEW_DEPENDENCY is removed as inapplicable.

title: Replay can hydrate from the GCS archive
statement: Replay must be able to hydrate partitions and read records from archived segments in Cloud Storage, through their manifests and replay indexes, once those segments are no longer on any broker.
rationale: Hot retention is hours to days for the market journal; a backtest or incident review older than that exists only if the archive is readable as a log.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-archive ('replay can hydrate from GCS')

verification.check: Let a partition's early segments age out of broker retention, replay the partition from offset zero, and assert the archived portion is read from the archive and the combined stream equals the original.

notes: Split from the fabric-archive row (stated twice in the raw extraction). G p23 §27's replay acceptance criterion, not in the raw extraction, depends on it. P0 because replay is master Phase 1 and the archive is in the GCP Phase 2 MVP.

title: Sinks isolate destination backpressure from the brokers
statement: Fabric sinks (fabric-sink-* for Bigtable, BigQuery, Spanner and GCS) must run as consumers outside the brokers, so a slow or failed destination backs up only that sink's consumer lag and never slows broker ingest or other consumers.
rationale: An analytics outage must not become a control outage; a sink inside the broker would pass its destination's backpressure straight onto P0 traffic.

sources.section: §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-sink-* ('Isolate destination backpressure from brokers')

verification.check: Freeze each destination fake in turn and assert broker append latency and other consumers' throughput are unchanged while only the frozen sink's lag grows (v2.1 §25 broker-backpressure game day).

notes: Split from the fabric-sink-* row (stated twice in the raw extraction); its restart/replay-by-offset clause is FABRIC-016 and isolation between sinks is FABRIC-097. NEW_DEPENDENCY moves to the destination-specific sinks (FABRIC-012, FABRIC-044, FABRIC-107, FABRIC-108).

title: Admin tooling moves partitions, drains leadership, repairs and compacts
statement: The fabric's admin/repair/rebalance component must be able, on every broker, to move partitions, drain leadership from a broker, enforce retention, repair under-replicated partitions and perform offline compaction.
rationale: Upgrades, scaling and recovery all need leadership to move deliberately; without these operations each becomes a failure injected on purpose.

VIEWS.fabric — 03 · Native Rust Event & Control Fabric, node 'f_admin' ('Partition moves, retention, repair, offline compaction')
